chunks: Muhammad ibn Ahmad ibn Yahya, from Muhammad ibn Isa, from al-Qasim ibn 'Urwa, from Zurara, from Abu Ja'far (peace be upon him) who said:
I said to him: A man vowed not to approach his wife for three months. He said: So he said: Oath of abstention (Ila') does not become established until he swears for more than four months.

key_terms.إِيلَاءٌ: Oath of abstention from conjugal relations
key_terms.يَقْرَبَ: To approach or have conjugal relations

ai.seo_question: What is the minimum duration required for an oath of abstention (Ila') to be legally valid in Shia fiqh?
ai.summary: In this hadith from al-Isfahani's chain, Imam al-Baqir (AS) clarifies the jurisprudential threshold for 'Ila', specifying that an oath of exactly three months does not trigger the legal status of Ila, which requires a duration exceeding four months. This distinction is crucial in Shia fiqh for determining when a wife gains the right to seek judicial separation or if the husband must choose between reconciliation and divorce. The ruling underscores the precision required in interpreting marital oaths to protect the wife's rights within the family structure.
